newsitem.title: USA: Delta Express seen rising above clouds.
newsitem.headline: Delta Express seen rising above clouds.

text.p: With the name of Delta Air Lines Inc standing behind it, the carrier's new Delta Express unit may be able to profit from the unfavorable climate in which other low-cost upstarts are now operating, analysts said.
Heightened concern over airline safety and more intense regulatory scrutiny of low-cost carriers "may be the perfect environment for Delta Express," said Glenn Engel, an analyst with Goldman Sachs.
"Since the ValuJet crash, low-cost carriers have struggled," Engel said, refering to the May crash of Valujet Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades, which killed all 110 passengers and crew on board.
"A year ago, people didn't care what airline they flew. But now, people are more safety conscious. They want a name they know," he said.
Earlier, industry experts cast doubt on Delta Express' chances, citing Continental Airlines failed CALite experiment and United Airlines's questionable success with Shuttle by United.
But some analysts now see consumers turning away from other low-cost start-ups and moving toward Delta Express, which combines name recognition and low fares.
Even though Delta Express will operate as a separate unit, consumers are likely to view the new service as being essentially the same as the main carrier, analysts said.

Delta Express, aimed at Florida-bound leisure travelers, will fare better than the 51 smaller carriers currently serving that market because of brand name recognition and Delta's frequent flyer program, said Susan Donofrio, an airline analyst with NatWest Securities.
Donofrio also expects Delta Express to do better than Continental's aborted CAlite venture, which suffered from poor market selection and consumer confusion about service and offerings, she said.
Edward Starkman of the Starkman Airline Report still views Delta Express with some skepticism, however
He considers the Delta Express venture to be a "very defensive move. They're staking out their turf as far as Southwest Airlines is concerned. The goal is to minimize losses," Starkman said.
Southwest Airlines Co currently operates 11 aircraft in Florida.

Starkman said the Shuttle by United has helped its parent company stem market share losses. Delta will likely follow United's lead by using Delta Express to prevent further erosion of its market share.
Delta said it expected Delta Express to be profitable from its first year, with minimal start-up costs.
